name: MO-04
label: Safe R

key_factors: District's R+21 partisan lean strongly favors Republicans
Alford holds a roughly 38-to-1 fundraising advantage over Herrera ($1.58M to $42K)
Prediction markets price a Republican win at about 96 percent
No public polls or expert ratings, and the challenger lacks resources to compete
model.rationale: The district's 21-point Republican lean, Alford's incumbency, and his overwhelming financial advantage leave no sign of a competitive race, while prediction markets near 96 percent Republican reinforce the picture. Herrera's minimal fundraising gives the Democrat little path to an upset.
model.watch: A late wave of Democratic outside spending or a major scandal involving Alford would be needed to make this competitive.
notes: No expert rater lists this race; treated as safe for the party holding the seat.
No usable general-election polls; forecast rests on fundamentals and expert ratings.

overview:
Missouri's 4th District is firmly Republican territory, with a partisan lean of about 21 points toward the GOP. Incumbent Mark Alford is seeking re-election with a decisive financial advantage, having raised roughly 1.6 million dollars and holding more than 770,000 dollars on hand. Democratic nominee Jordan Herrera has raised about 42,000 dollars, and a Libertarian candidate also appears on the ballot.

No public polls or expert ratings cover the race, so the outlook rests on district fundamentals, fundraising, and prediction markets, which price Alford's chances around 96 percent. With no evidence of a competitive challenge, the seat is rated Safe Republican, with Alford expected to win by roughly 19 points.
